extracted.intended_audience: law students, policymakers, adjudicators, lawyers and claimants interested in Canada Pension Plan (CPP) disability benefits and appeal procedures
extracted.subtask_description: Descriptive legal/accounting of the procedural, evidentiary, and substantive standards governing initial applications, administrative examination, Review Committees, Disability Determination Boards, decision-making, notification, and review for Canada Pension Plan disability and related benefits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Essential features of Review Committees
rubrics_metrics.description: Review Committees are a sort of people's appeal tribunal, constituted ad hoc of members designated on an equal basis by the litigants, with no permanent infrastructure and capable of sitting in any convenient place; their composition depends entirely on the will of the parties, the sole proviso of membership being Canadian resident status.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: One member nominated by dissatisfied applicant, one by the Director General, a third (Chairman) coopted by the other two or designated by a superior court judge if they disagree.

rubrics_metrics.name: Formation locus and exception for spouse-pension appeals
rubrics_metrics.description: Forming a Review Committee generally devolves upon the district office within whose territory the appellant resides; exception when appeal concerns surviving spouse's pension, in which case organizing is entrusted to the Appeals Section attached to central administration.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Appellant is expected to have identified the person he wishes to appoint when giving notice of intent to appeal, but appointment often occurs after the Appeals Section acknowledges receipt and outlines procedure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timeline and initial designations in forming a Review Committee
rubrics_metrics.description: Process often begins with designation, within fifteen days of receiving the notice of appeal, of a secretary and later of the committee member whose appointment devolves on the Minister.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Designation theoretically by Director General but in practice by head of the district office; head's role is to put members in touch and assist in choice of chairman.

rubrics_metrics.name: Impartiality and exclusion of officials from Review Committee membership
rubrics_metrics.description: Service instructions are explicit as to the need to select individuals whose impartiality is above suspicion; officials of the Department of National Health and Welfare are automatically barred and an attempt is made to avoid designating any federal civil service official.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Head of district office maintains a standing list of possible candidates of good reputation and varied backgrounds; categories considered suitable are listed (businessmen, retired professionals, social club directors, provincial/municipal officials, ministers of religion, school trustees, self-employed, experienced housewives).

rubrics_metrics.name: Appointment and consent of Chairman
rubrics_metrics.description: Secretary invites the two members to meet and agree on appointment of a chairman within thirty days; if no agreement, Department suggests names and, if appellant remains adamant, head asks appellant's designated member to propose an acceptable name; chairman must have written consent from both committee members.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In practice secretary suggests individuals resident in the region who have already served on a Review Committee; written consent of both members must be obtained.

rubrics_metrics.name: Unpaid character of Review Committee service
rubrics_metrics.description: Neither the Chairman nor the members of the Review Committee are remunerated or compensated for their services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The unpaid nature makes the review mechanism inexpensive to operate — a deliberate design consideration of the legislator.

rubrics_metrics.name: Powers of the Review Committee
rubrics_metrics.description: The Committee may affirm or vary the Minister's decision, or take any action that might have been taken by the Minister himself; it has authority to decide any question of law or fact concerning the appellant's eligibility for benefits.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Committee's decision is conclusive as to the appellant's age; in other matters it is subject to appeal to the PAB; Committee may revise its own decision in light of new facts; it has no authority to substitute its own judgment for the Minister in the exercise of a discretionary power.

rubrics_metrics.name: Requirement to apply for pension benefit
rubrics_metrics.description: No pension benefit shall be payable to any person unless he has made an application for it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Application must be made by intended beneficiary or by a person empowered to do so on his behalf; application must be in writing and presented at a decentralized unit of the Department within the area of the applicant's residence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Department's duties on receipt of application
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department shall examine the application forthwith on receiving it and shall either approve payment and determine amount or decide that no payment is in order; a negative decision must be communicated to the applicant as soon as practicable and in writing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Section 91(1) authorizes Governor in Council to make regulations prescribing application manner, evidence, and procedures for dealing with and approving applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'disability' for disability pensions (section 43(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: Disability is defined as a state of 'severe and prolonged mental or physical disability.' Severity: must render the disabled person 'incapable regularly of pursuing any substantially gainful occupation.' Prolonged: likely to be long continued and of indefinite duration or likely to result in death.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluation of severity and duration requires medical expertise; PAB caselaw clarifies concept of 'severe' disability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Factors to consider and exclude in assessing disability
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluation must take into account individual factors such as age, aptitudes and professional training, but not economic or geographical circumstances such as availability of suitable jobs in the applicant's region.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessment of residual working capacity likewise requires specialized knowledge of nature and demands of types of employment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Continuing review requirement for disability-linked benefits
rubrics_metrics.description: Benefits tied to continuance of a claimant's disability require continuing review of entitlement because the beneficiary may cease to be disabled or dependency status may change.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The administrative process includes phases: initiation, examination, decision, and control of benefits.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application submission formality and required evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications must be in writing and use prescribed forms; application form must be accompanied by documents to enable authorities to check data, including a statement of earnings and contributions for the last two years; application must be sent/delivered to CPP district office within applicant's domicile territory.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prescribed forms arise from section 91(1) regulations and s.514 of CPP Regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Who may present application and representative authorization
rubrics_metrics.description: In principle application should be presented by the contributor himself; another person/body may be authorized to do so if they show the contributor is incapable of managing his affairs by reason of disability, sickness, insanity, or other cause, and Director General is satisfied federal/provincial law authorizes representative; otherwise DG appoints acceptable representative.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Representative must demonstrate authority; District office handles initial processing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Retroactivity limits on applications
rubrics_metrics.description: No application can have retroactive effect beyond the twelve-month period immediately preceding its presentation, with an exception for a disabled contributor who dies before submitting an application — representative may apply within a year of death, and application is presumed filed on day of death for retroactivity purposes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Analogous provision exists for person/institution having custody of disabled contributor's child to submit within a year of the child's death.

rubrics_metrics.name: Initial claimant questionnaire and in-person verification
rubrics_metrics.description: On receiving the application the district office dispatches a detailed questionnaire concerning nature/consequences of disability, treatment, occupational pursuit and earnings, training and experience; claimant must fill, sign, and return it; a CPP agent checks accuracy, meeting claimant in person if necessary and appending observations before transmitting to Ottawa.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This process dispenses claimant from necessity of obtaining medical report at this stage and allows personal contact between administration and applicant (decision-making authority does not take part at this stage).

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality and limited disclosure of application information
rubrics_metrics.description: Information furnished or gathered on an application is confidential and prevented from disclosure even to the courts except in prosecutions related to the application/execution of the CPP; may be disclosed to certain federal administrative authorities for CPP or UI Act purposes and to QPP/provincial authorities within limits; some info may be divulged at request of the individual.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unauthorized disclosure by an official makes him liable to criminal prosecution.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to withdraw an application after award
rubrics_metrics.description: Claimant retains right to withdraw his application for benefits up until the thirtieth day following the date of issue of the first cheque in payment of benefits, but must avail himself of this right prior to cashing the cheque and return the cheque to the Director General.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A favourable decision on the first application does not prejudice eligibility on subsequent applications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Division of responsibility in examination of disability applications
rubrics_metrics.description: Claims and Benefits Division handles sufficiency of contributions, determination of earnings, and checks on proofs of age/dependency; Disability Assessment Division addresses the central issue of the claimant's disability and assesses disability for other benefit types where relevant.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Disability examinations are subject to fairly elaborate regulations derived from s.91(1) (procedure for examination/approving claims, determination of disability, payment conditions, cost assumptions, treatment of refusal to submit to assessments).

rubrics_metrics.name: Disability Determination Board composition and advisory role
rubrics_metrics.description: Every pension application is referred to a Disability Determination Board composed of several staff-members of the Division, at least one of whom is a physician; the Board's task is to provide 'advice and assistance' to the Director General in determining whether payment is justified; Director General is obliged to 'consider' but is not bound by the Board's advice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In practice the Board's advice normally decides the event; Board examines information and may request medical reports if data are not sufficiently specific, clear or recent.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidence-gathering, specialist examination, and cost allocation
rubrics_metrics.description: If Board information is insufficient (~25% of cases), Board can require applicant to submit to a medical exam by a specialist designated by the Department; expenses incurred by claimant for such exams (including specialist fee) are borne by the CPP; with DG consent an advance may defray outlay; refusal to undergo exam leads to rejection for lack of conclusive evidence.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where disability results from workplace accident/occupational disease Board secures report from provincial workmen's compensation commission; 'reasonable' costs borne by CPP, 'unreasonable' costs due to claimant negligence/bad faith could be held against him.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of occupational rehabilitation specialists and employment profile
rubrics_metrics.description: Board must assess whether disability renders claimant incapable of pursuing substantially gainful occupation by examining physical/intellectual skills, training and occupational antecedents; occupational rehabilitation specialists construct an 'employment profile' describing claimant's capacity and a list of occupations whose skill requirements correspond with his abilities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assessment of work capacity is largely theoretical — established in terms of potential for hypothetical job requirements rather than actual availability of employment in claimant's area.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contents of Board recommendation and practice on reasons
rubrics_metrics.description: Board's recommendation to the Director General gives opinion on: the claimant's disability as of application date; date of onset within the twelve-month period preceding the application; state of disability at time of report or date ceased; practicability of requiring reasonable rehabilitation measures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Act does not require Board to give reasons for its opinion, but in practice reasons are invariably given and serve for all practical purposes as the Director General's own; Director General retains theoretical freedom to disregard Board's conclusions and obtain other expert opinion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Notification, form-letter content and clarity of appeal information
rubrics_metrics.description: Department's decision must be notified to claimant in writing by standardized bilingual form-letter; Notice of Entitlement (favourable) contains information and warnings about obligations to inform district office of termination of disability or changes in activity/earnings; negative decision uses more elaborate form advising of Board recommendation and referring to 'Statement of Disability Assessment' and instructing how to request reconsideration or appeal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Wording of notice may be ambiguous and could create impression of two distinct courses: informal request for reconsideration and formal appeal under section 83; Statement of Disability Assessment often paraphrases section 43(2) and may be obscure for laymen though medical analysis tends to be clearer.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pension amount calculation and interim payments
rubrics_metrics.description: Amount of pension payable is determined on basis of computerized data on applicant's earnings obtained from Department of National Revenue; if delays make final calculation impossible at decision time, Director General may fix amount of interim benefits to be adjusted once final calculation has been made.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Director General may also determine to what person or institution benefits of a claimant incapable of managing his affairs shall be paid.

rubrics_metrics.name: Review/amendment of decisions on the ground of new facts (section 86(2))
rubrics_metrics.description: Review of decisions on the ground of new facts is envisaged; review may take place whether new facts are presented by beneficiary or discovered by Department — initial decision may be amended upon initiative of either party.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A refused claimant is always free to adduce new facts to substantiate his claim, even long after the initial decision, without submitting a new application.
